The recent correlation reading of +0.50 between gold and Bitcoin is the highest since 2020, as Bitwise reported on September 3 using Bloomberg data from April 2015 through the end of August. U.S. stock futures were lower early Tuesday as rising Treasury yields, geopolitical friction and concerns around a potential slowdown in AI development weighed on investor sentiment ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision this week.

Quick Read

JEPQ's option-driven distributions hit ordinary income rates, costing high-bracket investors roughly $212 more per $10,000 annually than qualified dividends.

JEPQ's covered-call overlay capped returns at 19% over the past year while QQQM delivered 23% with lower fees and tax-friendlier distributions.

GPIQ and SPYI run similar monthly-income overlays structured to route distributions through return of capital or Section 1256 treatment, shrinking the tax bill.

Read More: Learn 7 ways to generate income with a $1,000,000+ portfolio (sponsor)

The deposit lands the first week of each month. It looks like income. Your 1099-DIV agrees, and so does the IRS: nearly every dollar JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income ETF (NASDAQ:JEPQ) sends you is taxed at your ordinary income rate, the same bracket that your paycheck is taxed.

Summit Art Creations / Shutterstock.com
What You're Actually Paying the IRS

JEPQ distributed $6.76379 per share over the trailing 12 months, paid across 12 monthly installments. With the ETF closing at $59.81 on September 11, 2026, a $10,000 stake produced roughly $1,131 in cash hitting the account over the year.

Here is the mechanism the marketing material skips. JEPQ generates most of that yield through equity-linked notes (ELNs) that pay a premium for writing short call options against the Nasdaq-100. Option and ELN premiums fail the IRS test for qualified dividend income and flow to your 1099-DIV as ordinary income. On roughly $1,131 of distributions, a high-bracket investor can owe about $377 in federal tax, versus roughly $165 had the same cash arrived as a qualified dividend or long-term capital gain. That is a $212 annual gap per $10,000, every year, in a taxable account. Stack that gap for two decades and the after-tax drag runs into the low four figures per $10,000, before touching the fund's expense ratio.

Covered-Call Cap Buried in the Factsheet

Tax treatment is only half the quiet cost. JEPQ's short-call overlay pays for the monthly check by selling away upside. When the Nasdaq rallies aggressively, JEPQ collects the option premium and hands the gains above the strike to the option buyer. The returns show it. Over the past year, JEPQ returned 18.96% while the plain Nasdaq-100 tracked by Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ) returned 22.45%. Year to date through September 11, JEPQ managed 11.47% against QQQ's 16.42%. Every point of that gap is money the overlay sold for premium that ends up taxed at your ordinary wage rate.

The S&P 500 ended Monday 0.5% lower, while the Nasdaq 100 slipped 0.8% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average eased 0.3%. The Russell 2000, which tracks stocks with small market capitalizations, fell about 0.4%.

In a 3,800-word essay, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei advocated moderating the pace of cutting-edge AI development to mitigate safety risks and prevent superintelligent systems from escaping human authority. The statement gained backing from top industry leaders, including OpenAI's Sam Altman and SpaceXAI's Elon Musk.

Adding to AI safety needs, Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) unveiled a draft policy on Monday governing the development of its frontline artificial intelligence models, explicitly mandating that its systems remain subordinate to human oversight and rejecting the pursuit of unchecked, fully autonomous superintelligence.

"What really happened? Surely something big enough to spook Dario, Sam, and Elon into rare agreement," Giuseppe Sette at Reflexivity told Bloomberg in an interview. "Whatever it was, it was probably stopped at the last minute, just before disaster struck. With China in the race, though, we don't expect any major slowdown."

In commodity markets, crude prices advanced following Saudi Arabia's shutdown of a crucial pipeline bypassing the Strait of Hormuz, though gains moderated later in the session. West Texas Intermediate futures gained 1.3% to finish at $101.39 a barrel, while Brent crude rose 1% to settle at $105.68. Meanwhile, U.S. Treasury yields also continued last week's climb.
